note: Every Minecraft version, by era: the Java it runs on, the loaders a mod or plugin can target (eras/loaders.json names each loader's packages and where its declared compatibility lives), how its code is named (names.dev: what the source is written in; names.runtime: what the running game is called, per loader, '*' for the rest), the Java a loader's scanner reads (outerJava), and the walls a port crosses. Read by the Gradle plugin (mycelium { minecraft = ... }): a target's era sets its Java, its era gate and its evidence; an artifact's declared range is held to the walls (docs/decisions/0009). Ordered newest first; from and to are inclusive, and each is a version as Mojang's launcher manifest names it (eras/versions.json) or a whole line, '<line>.x' (every version of that line, those still to come included). A loader listed in an era exists on every version of it unless 'since' gives the first version it exists on. A wall is the first version of its far side: 'at' is a real version, 'for' names the loaders or families ('mod', 'plugin') it splits (absent: every artifact), and a range holding a wall needs a proof version on each side (docs/decisions/0009). 'notes' are facts that are not walls. The repository check proves every real version falls in exactly one era and every named version, loader and name is real. 'realizations' holds one more table per divide over the same versions, each ordered newest first, that no era row can hold because its ranges cross the eras: what a version realizes the divide as (item.presentation: how an item's state is drawn, item-definition, model-overrides or none, read by the item.presentation compiler; item.carrier: where a stack keeps its state, custom-data, root-tag or none, read by the item-carrier bridge), 'none' meaning the game cannot do it there (decision 0016); every real version falls in exactly one range of every table. 'packFormat' is a third table over the same versions, newest first, of the resource-pack and data-pack format each range of versions has (the game's own version.json pack_version; a minor from 1.21.9 is written major.minor): the Gradle plugin writes a target's pack.mcmeta from it (docs/decisions/0017). Each row's 'source' says where it was read: a real game jar ('jar <version>', its version.json) or minecraft.wiki's Pack format table ('wiki'); resource packs begin at 1.6.1, data packs at 1.13. Each row's facts are re-verified against the loaders' own mavens when a consumer first ports to it (docs/eras.md).

item.presentation.what: an item definition (items/<id>.json) selects a model, here on the custom_model_data strings
one item model with overrides on the custom_model_data predicate, a float that must be written in ascending order
no custom model data: nothing draws an item by its state

item.carrier.what: the stack's state is the minecraft:custom_data component (CustomData); an empty one is no component at all
the stack's state is its root tag (ItemStack.getTag / setTag); an empty one is a null tag, since a null and an empty tag do not stack
the bridge is written in Mojang's names, which the game's own mappings give from 1.14.4 (a variant in the older names could cover these)

world.clock.what: the game has world clocks: ServerClockManager holds each clock's state, timelines (data) lay periods and markers over a clock, and the game syncs clocks to clients itself
the game has one clock, dayTime: the overworld clock is that, and a mod's own clocks are held in saved data, advanced on the server tick and synced by the mod's payload
the bridge is written in Mojang's names, which the game's own mappings give from 1.14.4 (a variant in the older names could cover these)

state.lifecycle.what: a player and the server cross by the loader's events (login, logout, the copy to a respawned player, death, a dimension change, a save, the server's start and stop); durable values live in the overworld's saved data, a SavedDataType with a codec

the bridge's loader halves are written against the events of 1.21 to 1.21.1 and of 26.3 on (Fabric API, NeoForge and Forge as they are there), and the versions between are not read: a mod that targets one writes this half itself, or the half is added here when it has been read and built on that version
